title: Fixed lunar periods reduced high-water error and cross-coast tail concurrence at six US gauges in 2011-2025
abstract: We tested a tide explanation for shared high-water dates at six US gauges. We fitted fixed lunar periods to daily maximum water level minus monthly mean in 1996-2010 and tested the fits in 2011-2025. The lunar model reduced mean squared error by 16.6% to 77.4% against a seasonal model. An equal-size control model with other periods raised error at all six gauges. Average same-date upper-tail concurrence across eight Atlantic-Pacific pairs fell from 1.104% to 0.271%. The paired conditional 95% interval for the change was -1.069 to -0.632 percentage points. Mean excess above a blocked year-pairing reference fell from 0.699 to -0.007 points. All eight cross-coast pairs passed the adjusted excess test before the lunar fit; none passed after it. Five same-coast pairs still passed. This supports a tide explanation for much of the cross-coast pattern. It does not isolate storm surge or prove a physical cause. Thresholds use the test-period distribution. The model fit alone uses earlier data. The intervals fix fitted models and thresholds. The package gives source hashes, daily evidence, predictions, code, reference draws, a figure, and source and count audits.

display.caption: Left: error reduction in 2011-2025 for fixed fits from 1996-2010, with conditional three-year block intervals. Right: same-date upper-tail rates for all 15 gauge pairs. Thresholds are fitted separately within the evaluation period.
